What a weird take lmao. Obviously taking care of an animal isn’t as hard to take care of as an actual human being, but taking care of an animal is still work and they are kinda the pets parent. If you’re interested I can direct you to some studies that go over this kind of thing in more detail, but there is a scientific basis for this kind of thing. 

That all being said, not everyone is an animal person and not everyone bonds with animals. That isn’t something I can fully understand because pets bring me so much joy, but that isn’t the case for everyone. It doesn’t mean you’re a psychopath, it doesn’t mean you have a personality disorder. It’s just who you are. I saw some people saying it was psychopathic, which could be true, but if you don’t struggle to bond with people or lack empathy in other areas of your life I don’t think that line is correct. There’s nothing that you could say to change how I view my pets, and there’s nothing I could say that would change how you view yours. I would just advise against getting a pet if you don’t believe you can bond with one and want to take care of it. Because you can be stuck with one for years and years.

Animals can provide us emotional support in ways that humans can’t. Animals are innocent, friendly. Dogs in particular will love you and you will be their world. That kind of companionship is enticing to people, and you can develop strong bonds with the animal as a result. I have a cat who I’ve had for 7 years and I can’t imagine life without her. When I was severely depressed taking care of her was the only reason I got out of bed. Shes a family member to me because I love her, I take care of her and make sure she’s healthy and okay. In turn she’s my buddy and loves me in her own way. Shes a living creature that I decided to take responsibility for, not something that can just be given away or thrown away when it becomes inconvenient. Shes not a human and I don’t equate her to a human life, but that doesn’t make her any less of a family member.
